chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Shihab ibn 'Abd Rabbih, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a junub: may he wash the deceased? Or if someone has washed a deceased person, may he go to his family, then perform ghusl?

He said: “They are the same. There is no harm in that. If he is junub, he should wash his hands, perform wudu (ablution), and wash the deceased while he is junub. And if he has washed a deceased person, then goes to his family, he should perform wudu (ablution), then go to his family, and one ghusl suffices him for both.”

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: his wife or family, here referring to his spouse
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.غُسْلٌ وَاحِدٌ: a single ghusl that is sufficient for both causes
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُ: washes, specifically the ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: Can a junub wash a deceased person, and is one ghusl enough if someone washes a deceased and then goes to his spouse?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity in two related cases: a person in janabah washing a deceased body, and a person who washed a deceased then has relations with his spouse before ghusl. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that both cases are alike, permits the action with prior wudu (ablution), and rules that one ghusl suffices for both causes.
